title: Victim loses £250k after scammers use AI video of 'well-known' celebrity

reading.body:
This is an impersonation failure, and the synthetic video is the part that does the work. An AI generated video appearing to feature a well known figure from the financial sector was used to advertise an investment with large returns, which gave a fraudulent offer the credibility of a recognised name. The video did not take anyone's money by itself. It opened the door.

The loss happened after that opening, in a sequence that moved off the video and onto WhatsApp, where the victim was urged to pay more, then into remote access to the victim's computer granted under the claim of help with the investment, then into multiple online accounts and borrowed money sent to accounts controlled by criminals. Catching it would have required the check the police later described, which is independent verification of who the victim was dealing with and confirmation that the financial services provider was authorised by the Financial Conduct Authority. That check sits outside the video and outside the platform, at the point where a person decides whether the counterparty is real.

What is not established is who the video depicted. The police did not name the person, and the similar scams BBC News NI has seen involving named financial figures are not a finding that any of those people were involved in this case or consented to anything.

reports.title: Victim loses £250k after scammers use AI video of 'well-known' celebrity

summary:
A person in the Ards and north Down area lost £250,000 in a scam involving an AI generated video, according to the Police Service of Northern Ireland. The video appeared to feature a well known person from the financial sector and advertised an investment with large returns. Police did not name the celebrity, but BBC News NI has seen similar scams using financial experts Martin Lewis, Peter Jones and Steven Bartlett. After a small initial investment, the victim was contacted on WhatsApp and urged to pay more.

Fraudsters persuaded the victim to open multiple online accounts and gained remote access to their computer by claiming to help with the investment. Police called it a complex and large fraud. The victim was encouraged to borrow money, and funds were sent to accounts controlled by criminals. Police advised people to independently verify who they are dealing with and check that financial services providers are authorised by the Financial Conduct Authority. Superintendent Joanne Gibson also urged people to stop and check financial activity and for families to talk about fraud.
title_en: Victim loses £250k after scammers use AI video of 'well-known' celebrity
